entries.name: Screen
entries.summary: Text-mode drawing on the base layer: text, boxes, fills, block moves, lines, shades, progress bars, and pixel helpers for mode 10.
entries.description: Text-mode drawing on the base layer: text, boxes, fills, block moves, lines, shades, progress bars, and pixel helpers for mode 10. Region calls take inclusive corners (x1, y1, x2, y2). Constants: Screen.COLS/ROWS (the current mode's 40x30 or 80x60), the modes Screen.TEXT40 .. Screen.PIXELS, Screen.SINGLE, Screen.DOUBLE, Screen.INVERT (0x80). The Attributes namespace (part of this framework) names the colours and the inverse bit for attr arguments.

entries.name: Attributes
entries.summary: Attribute values by name for the attr argument of every Screen and Overlay call: colours plus Attributes.Inverse.
entries.description: An attribute byte is a colour index (bits 0-2) plus the inverse bit (0x80). Attributes.Red .. Attributes.Orange are the mode-1 default palette entries 1-8 (Screen.Palette recolours them); Attributes.Inverse swaps text and background, so a space with Attributes.Blue + Attributes.Inverse is a solid blue block. Add a colour and Inverse together; never add two colours. Defined by the Screen framework, used by Overlay calls too.
entries.example: Screen.Fill(2, 3, 37, 3, 32, Attributes.Red + Attributes.Inverse)  -- a red bar

entries.name: Overlay
entries.summary: The same drawing calls on the overlay layer, composited over the base: dialogs, menus, HUDs.
entries.description: The same drawing calls on the overlay layer, composited over the base: dialogs, menus, HUDs. Cells you write show, untouched cells stay transparent, Overlay.Clear() hides everything. Constants as Screen.

entries.name: Text
entries.summary: String helpers for a 40-column screen: alignment and padding, truncation, word wrap, splitting and joining, zero-padding and thousands separators..
entries.description: String helpers for a 40-column screen: alignment and padding, truncation, word wrap, splitting and joining, zero-padding and thousands separators.

entries.name: Timer
entries.summary: Timer objects with an id: one-shots (After) and repeats (Every) that can be cancelled, paused, resumed and restarted.
entries.description: Timer objects with an id: one-shots (After) and repeats (Every) that can be cancelled, paused, resumed and restarted. Methods on the object (t:Pause()) and functions (Timer.Pause(t) or Timer.Pause(t.id)) are the same. Built on the OS's 8 timers per program.

entries.name: Sound
entries.summary: Built-in instruments and effects by name, tones and noise, and your own sounds.
entries.description: A bank of built-in sounds is baked into the OS: instruments (lead, pulse, bass, piano, organ, strings, flute, brass, bell, pluck, chime, kick, snare, hihat, tom, clap) and effects (coin, jump, laser, zap, explosion, hit, hurt, powerup, blip, select, error, alarm, engine, splash, bounce, teleport). Sound.Effect plays an effect at its own pitch, Sound.Play an instrument at a note; Sound.Define makes your own from a waveform, an ADSR envelope and pitch/tone effects (slide, vibrato, arpeggio, cutoff), or from a built-in as `base`. 8 effect voices play beside the 8 tune channels.

entries.name: Music
entries.summary: Tunes written as notes (MML) on up to 8 channels of built-in or own sounds, played by name and looped.
entries.description: Music.Track compiles MML strings (notes, lengths, octaves, tempo, volume, ties, repeats) into a score the engine plays on its 8 tune channels; Music.Define takes event tables directly. One tune plays at a time; effects play over it.
entries.example:
Music.Track("theme", { tempo = 120, loop = true, channels = { { sound = "lead", mml = "o4 l8 c d e f g a b > c" } } })
Music.Play("theme")

entries.name: Sound.Tone
entries.summary: Plays a square-wave tone at (nearest note to) `hz` for `ms` milliseconds; `volume` 0..255 (default 255).
entries.description: Plays a square-wave tone at (nearest note to) `hz` for `ms` milliseconds; `volume` 0..255 (default 255). Returns the voice id.

entries.name: Sound.Beep
entries.summary: A short 880 Hz beep (default 80 ms).
entries.description: A short 880 Hz beep (default 80 ms).

entries.name: Sound.Noise
entries.summary: A burst of noise for `ms` milliseconds (explosions, hits).
entries.description: A burst of noise for `ms` milliseconds (explosions, hits).

entries.name: Sound.Effect
entries.summary: Plays a built-in effect at its own pitch: "coin", "jump", "laser", "zap", "explosion", "hit", "hurt", "powerup", "blip", "select", "error", "alarm", "engine", "splash", "bounce", "teleport" (the instruments work too, at C4).
entries.description: Plays a built-in effect at its own pitch: "coin", "jump", "laser", "zap", "explosion", "hit", "hurt", "powerup", "blip", "select", "error", "alarm", "engine", "splash", "bounce", "teleport" (the instruments work too, at C4). Returns the voice id.

entries.name: Sound.Play
entries.summary: Plays a sound: a built-in name ("piano", "laser"), an id from Sound.Define or Sound.Load, at `note` (a MIDI number or a name such as "C4"; default: the sound's own note); `ms` 0 or none means the sound's own envelope; volume 0..255, pan -64..63.
entries.description: Plays a sound: a built-in name ("piano", "laser"), an id from Sound.Define or Sound.Load, at `note` (a MIDI number or a name such as "C4"; default: the sound's own note); `ms` 0 or none means the sound's own envelope; volume 0..255, pan -64..63. Returns the voice id.

entries.name: Sound.Instrument
entries.summary: The id of a built-in sound, for scores and Music.Track channels.
entries.description: The id of a built-in sound, for scores and Music.Track channels.

entries.name: Sound.Presets
entries.summary: The built-in sounds: a list of { name, effect, id }, or with `effects` true only the effects, false only the instruments.
entries.description: The built-in sounds: a list of { name, effect, id }, or with `effects` true only the effects, false only the instruments.
entries.example: for _, p in ipairs(Sound.Presets(true)) do print(p.name) end  -- the effects

entries.name: Sound.Spec
entries.summary: A built-in sound's definition as a spec table, to change and give to Sound.Define (or use `base` there).
entries.description: A built-in sound's definition as a spec table, to change and give to Sound.Define (or use `base` there).
entries.example:
local spec = Sound.Spec("laser")
spec.slide = -900
Sound.Define(0, spec)

entries.name: Sound.Define
entries.summary: Defines a sound of your own under id 0..29 (30 and 31 are Tone and Noise): spec = { base = "built-in name" (start from it), wave = "square"|"triangle"|"saw"|"sine"|"noise", duty = 1..15, attack, decay, release = ms, sustain = 0..255, volume = 0..255, note = "C5", slide = semitones per second, vibrato = cents, vibrato_rate = Hz, arp, arp2 = semitone steps, arp_ms = ms per step, arp_loop = true to cycle, cutoff = 0..255 (255 open, lower darker) }; every field is optional.
entries.description: Defines a sound of your own under id 0..29 (30 and 31 are Tone and Noise): spec = { base = "built-in name" (start from it), wave = "square"|"triangle"|"saw"|"sine"|"noise", duty = 1..15, attack, decay, release = ms, sustain = 0..255, volume = 0..255, note = "C5", slide = semitones per second, vibrato = cents, vibrato_rate = Hz, arp, arp2 = semitone steps, arp_ms = ms per step, arp_loop = true to cycle, cutoff = 0..255 (255 open, lower darker) }; every field is optional.

entries.name: Sound.Load
entries.summary: Loads a WAV from the card as an instrument, with the note it was recorded at.
entries.description: Loads a WAV file from the card (8/16-bit PCM, mono or stereo, up to 48 kHz, 64 KB of samples a program) as an instrument: `root` is the note the recording is of ("C2" for a bass sampled at C2; default C4), and playing any other note shifts the pitch by the difference, so a single recording covers the scale. Returns a sound id for Sound.Play and Music.Track channels.

entries.name: Sound.Stop
entries.summary: Stops one voice returned by a Play call, or every one-shot voice.
entries.description: Stops one voice returned by a Play call, or every one-shot voice.

entries.name: Sound.Volume
entries.summary: Sets the master volume 0..255.
entries.description: Sets the master volume 0..255.

entries.name: Music.Track
entries.summary: Defines a tune from notes: spec = { tempo = 120, loop = true, channels = { { sound = "lead", mml = "..." }, .
entries.description: Defines a tune from notes: spec = { tempo = 120, loop = true, channels = { { sound = "lead", mml = "..." }, ... } } with up to 8 channels, each a built-in name or a sound id and an MML string: c d e f g a b  notes (# or + sharp, - flat); a number after a note is its length (4 quarter, 8 eighth, 1 whole; a dot adds half), else the default length r or p         a rest (with a length like a note) l8             default length; o4 octave; > < octave up/down t120           tempo in beats a minute; v0..v15 volume (each channel starts at 16 / sqrt(channels), capped at 15, so a full mix does not clip); q1..q8 how much of a note sounds (q8 legato, q4 staccato) c4&c8          a tie joins two notes;  [ c d e ]3  repeats three times Spaces and bar lines are ignored. On a drum or effect channel (a sound with a pitch of its own, like "kick") every note is a hit at that pitch, so "c c r c" is a rhythm. Returns true (and the compiled score), or nil, err.

entries.name: Music.Define
entries.summary: Defines a score from events: { loop = bool, channels = { { { at = ms, sound = name|id, note = "C4", dur = ms, vol = 0..255, pan = -64..63 }, .
entries.description: Defines a score from events: { loop = bool, channels = { { { at = ms, sound = name|id, note = "C4", dur = ms, vol = 0..255, pan = -64..63 }, ... }, ... } } (see lua.md). Music.Track is the easier way.
entries.example: Music.Define("tune", { loop = true, channels = { { { at = 0, sound = "lead", note = "C4", dur = 200 } } } })

entries.name: Music.Play
entries.summary: Starts a defined tune; `loop` overrides the tune's own loop flag.
entries.description: Starts a defined tune; `loop` overrides the tune's own loop flag.

entries.name: Music.Stop
entries.summary: Stops the tune that is playing.
entries.description: Stops the tune that is playing.

entries.name: Music.Playing
entries.summary: True while a tune is playing.
entries.description: True while a tune is playing.
entries.example: if not Music.Playing() then Music.Play("theme") end

entries.name: Graphics
entries.summary: Pixels, shapes, sprites (rotation, flips, scaling), scrolling and text on the pixel modes 10 (320x240) and 11 (160x120).
entries.description: One palette byte per pixel; every drawing call is one display op, clipped by the display core. Images are strings of w*h palette bytes (Graphics.Pixels builds one from ASCII art); Rotate, Flip and Scale make new images in Lua, so build frames once and keep them. Sprites are objects with Draw/Hide/MoveTo/MoveBy/SetImage/Turn methods and x, y, w, h fields. Constants: Graphics.WIDTH/HEIGHT for the current mode, and the sixteen text colours by name (Graphics.BLACK .. Graphics.LIGHTGREY).
entries.example:
Graphics.Mode(11)
local px, w, h = Graphics.Pixels({ ".X.", "XXX", ".X." }, { X = Graphics.YELLOW })
local s = Graphics.Sprite(w, h, px, 0)
s:Draw(80, 60)

entries.name: Graphics.Mode
entries.summary: Selects pixel mode 10 (320x240, the default) or 11 (160x120), clearing the screen to colour 0, and sets Graphics.WIDTH/HEIGHT.
entries.description: Selects pixel mode 10 (320x240, the default) or 11 (160x120), clearing the screen to colour 0, and sets Graphics.WIDTH/HEIGHT. Pixel modes have no text cells: Graphics.Text draws text as pixels.

entries.name: Graphics.Text
entries.signature: Graphics.Text(x, y, text, colour [, bg [, scale]])
entries.summary: Text as pixels with the 8x8 font (or the program's own tiles), from pixel (x, y): 8 pixels a character, or 8 * scale with `scale` 2-4.
entries.description: Text as pixels with the 8x8 font (or the program's own tiles), from pixel (x, y): 8 pixels a character, or 8 * scale with `scale` 2-4. With `bg` each character's cell is painted first; without it only the letters are drawn over what is there. One op.
entries.example:
Graphics.Text(4, 4, "SCORE 120", Graphics.WHITE, Graphics.BLACK)
Graphics.Text(20, 40, "GO!", Graphics.YELLOW, nil, 3)

entries.name: Graphics.TextWidth
entries.summary: The width in pixels Graphics.Text gives `text`: 8 * scale a character.
entries.description: The width in pixels Graphics.Text gives `text`: 8 * scale a character.

entries.name: Graphics.CenterText

entries.description: Graphics.Text centred across the screen on pixel row y.

entries.name: Graphics.Blit
entries.signature: Graphics.Blit(x, y, w, h, pixels [, key])
entries.summary: Copies a w by h image, `pixels` a string of w*h palette bytes row by row, to (x, y).
entries.description: Copies a w by h image, `pixels` a string of w*h palette bytes row by row, to (x, y). With `key`, pixels of that colour are transparent. An image over 8184 pixels is sent in bands of rows (one op each).

entries.name: Graphics.Scroll
entries.summary: Shifts the whole screen by (dx, dy) pixels (-127..127); the pixels uncovered get `fill` (default 0).
entries.description: Shifts the whole screen by (dx, dy) pixels (-127..127); the pixels uncovered get `fill` (default 0). One op: a scrolling backdrop costs one Scroll plus drawing the new edge.
entries.example: Graphics.Scroll(-1, 0)  -- the backdrop moves left a pixel

entries.name: Graphics.ScrollRect
entries.signature: Graphics.ScrollRect(x, y, w, h, dx, dy [, fill])
entries.summary: Shifts the pixels of one rectangle by (dx, dy); pixels uncovered inside it get `fill` (default 0).
entries.description: Shifts the pixels of one rectangle by (dx, dy); pixels uncovered inside it get `fill` (default 0).

entries.name: Graphics.RGB
entries.summary: The palette index nearest a colour (each 0-255) in the default palette's 6x6x6 cube (entries 16-231).
entries.description: The palette index nearest a colour (each 0-255) in the default palette's 6x6x6 cube (entries 16-231).

entries.name: Graphics.Grey
entries.summary: The palette index nearest a grey (0 black .
entries.description: The palette index nearest a grey (0 black .. 255 white): the default palette's grey ramp (entries 232-255), or black or white.

entries.name: Graphics.Palette
entries.summary: Sets palette entry `index` (0-255) to a colour; everything drawn in that index changes at once (palette animation).
entries.description: Sets palette entry `index` (0-255) to a colour; everything drawn in that index changes at once (palette animation). Entries 0-8 are also the text colours.

entries.name: Graphics.Pixels
entries.summary: Builds an image from ASCII art: `rows` a list of equal-length strings, `map` a table from character to colour; characters not in the map become `key` (default 0).
entries.description: Builds an image from ASCII art: `rows` a list of equal-length strings, `map` a table from character to colour; characters not in the map become `key` (default 0). Returns pixels, w, h for Blit or Sprite.
entries.example: local px, w, h = Graphics.Pixels({ ".XX.", "XXXX", ".XX." }, { X = Graphics.WHITE })

entries.name: Graphics.Rotate
entries.summary: A copy of a w x h image turned `angle` degrees clockwise.
entries.description: A copy of a w x h image turned `angle` degrees clockwise. 90, 180 and 270 keep every pixel (the result is h x w for 90 and 270); any other angle gives a square image big enough for the turned shape, the gaps filled with `key` (default 0). Returns pixels, w, h.
entries.example: local turned, tw, th = Graphics.Rotate(px, w, h, 45, 0)

entries.name: Graphics.Flip
entries.summary: A mirrored copy of an image: left-right when `horizontal` is true, top-bottom when `vertical` is (both by default).
entries.description: A mirrored copy of an image: left-right when `horizontal` is true, top-bottom when `vertical` is (both by default). Returns pixels.
entries.example: local mirrored = Graphics.Flip(px, w, h, true, false)

entries.name: Graphics.Scale
entries.summary: An image enlarged by a whole `factor` (2 doubles every pixel).
entries.description: An image enlarged by a whole `factor` (2 doubles every pixel). Returns pixels, w * factor, h * factor.
entries.example: local big, bw, bh = Graphics.Scale(px, w, h, 2)

entries.name: Graphics.Sprite
entries.summary: A sprite object for a w x h image (`pixels` as for Blit).
entries.description: A sprite object for a w x h image (`pixels` as for Blit). `key` is its transparent colour. Show it with s:Draw(x, y), move it with s:MoveTo(x, y) (which repaints what it uncovers with s.background: a colour, default 0, or a function(x, y, w, h) that redraws that area), change its picture with s:SetImage or s:Turn. Fields: x, y, w, h.
entries.example:
local ship = Graphics.Sprite(w, h, px, 0)
ship:Draw(70, 50)

entries.name: Graphics.Draw
entries.summary: Draws the sprite at (x, y) (default: where it is), without erasing anything: use it to show a sprite, or to redraw one after the screen was cleared or scrolled.
entries.description: Draws the sprite at (x, y) (default: where it is), without erasing anything: use it to show a sprite, or to redraw one after the screen was cleared or scrolled.

entries.name: Graphics.Hide
entries.summary: Removes the sprite: its area is repainted with its background.
entries.description: Removes the sprite: its area is repainted with its background.

entries.name: Graphics.MoveTo
entries.summary: Moves the sprite: the old area is repainted with its background, then the sprite is drawn at (x, y).
entries.description: Moves the sprite: the old area is repainted with its background, then the sprite is drawn at (x, y). Two ops; nothing happens when it has not moved.

entries.name: Graphics.MoveBy
entries.summary: Moves the sprite by (dx, dy) pixels: MoveTo relative to where it is.
entries.description: Moves the sprite by (dx, dy) pixels: MoveTo relative to where it is.

entries.name: Graphics.SetImage
entries.summary: Gives the sprite a new picture (an animation frame); a shown sprite is redrawn in place, erased first if the size changed.
entries.description: Gives the sprite a new picture (an animation frame); a shown sprite is redrawn in place, erased first if the size changed. The picture also becomes the one Turn rotates.

entries.name: Graphics.Turn
entries.summary: Shows the sprite's picture rotated `angle` degrees clockwise (from its unrotated image, so angles do not add up), keeping the rotated images so a repeated angle costs nothing: round angles to a step (say 15 degrees) to bound the memory.
entries.description: Shows the sprite's picture rotated `angle` degrees clockwise (from its unrotated image, so angles do not add up), keeping the rotated images so a repeated angle costs nothing: round angles to a step (say 15 degrees) to bound the memory. A shown sprite is redrawn, centred where it was.

entries.name: Graphics.Overlaps
entries.summary: True when two sprites' rectangles overlap (a simple hit test).
entries.description: True when two sprites' rectangles overlap (a simple hit test).
entries.example: if Graphics.Overlaps(ship, rock) then explode() end

entries.name: Graphics.OnScreen
entries.summary: True while any part of the sprite is inside the screen.
entries.description: True while any part of the sprite is inside the screen.
entries.example: if not ship:OnScreen() then respawn() end

entries.name: Graphics.WIDTH

entries.name: Graphics.HEIGHT
entries.summary: Pixels down in the current mode: 240 (mode 10) or 120 (mode 11).

entries.summary: Palette index 6: blue in the default palette.

entries.name: Screen.Mode
entries.summary: Selects a screen mode and updates Screen.COLS/ROWS (and Graphics.WIDTH/HEIGHT); switching clears the screen.
entries.description: 0 (Screen.TEXT40) 40x30 B&W, 1 (TEXT40C) 40x30 colour, 2 (TEXT80) 80x60 B&W, 3 (TEXT80C) 80x60 colour, 10 (PIXELS) 320x240 pixels, 11 (PIXELS_LO) 160x120 pixels. The 80-column modes draw at the full 640x480 and cost the display core about four times the rendering per line; the pixel modes have no text cells (the Graphics framework draws there, text included). Sets Screen.COLS/ROWS and Overlay.COLS/ROWS, and Graphics.WIDTH/HEIGHT when that framework is loaded.

entries.name: Screen.Clear
entries.summary: Fills the whole base layer with `char` (default space) and attribute 0.
entries.description: Fills the whole base layer with `char` (default space) and attribute 0.

entries.description: Writes one character code at a cell.

entries.description: Sets one cell's attribute, keeping its character.

entries.description: A blank window: the inside cleared, a frame around it and an optional title on the top edge.

entries.description: Calls fn(timer) once, `ms` milliseconds from now. Returns the timer.

entries.description: Re-arms a timer from now with its interval (or a new one), whether it was running, paused or already fired. Returns the timer.
